body_text:
Let $D_1,\ldots,D_n$ be domains. An $n$-ary predicate $P$ on
these domains is an expression for which $P(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ is
a statement whenever $a_i\in D_i$ for every $i$. Equivalently,
after a semantics has been fixed, $P$ determines a truth-valued
function on $D_1\times\cdots\times D_n$. The domains are part
of the specification: the same formula may define different
predicates when its variables range over different objects.
